question_record.context: A known credential theft tool execution command line was detected on host `vnevado-win10v`, involving processes such as `powershell.exe` and `mimikatz.exe`. The credential theft tool `mimikatz.exe` was executed with Process ID 4112 and the following command line: `mimikatz.exe privilege::debug sekurlsa::pth /user:kyleg /ntlm:96def1a633fc6790124d5f8fe31cc72b /domain:vnevado.alpineskihouse.co /run:"powershell.exe dir \vnevado-win10b\c$"` on the host. Subsequently, PsExec was used to launch a command on a remote device. There was also activity indicating the use of the Rubeus tool for potential kerberoasting attacks. Finally, a suspicious service was launched on the device during this sequence of events.
question_record.question: Can you provide the ProcessId, CreatedTime, and CommandLine for the suspicious service that was launched on the device?
solution: A known credential theft tool was executed on host `vnevado-win10v`.
The Rubeus kerberoasting tool was possibly used on process `psexesvc.exe` with Process ID `5512` and command line `psexesvc.exe` at `2024-06-27t14:33:27.3525354z`.
PsExec was launched to execute a command, saving output to `adminticket.txt`.

95.name: PsExec launched a command on a remote device

0.name: Possible use of the Rubeus kerberoasting tool
0.description:
Activity indicating the use of the Rubeus tool was observed on this endpoint. This tool can perform kerberoasting, pass-the-ticket, and other attack techniques that take advantage of Kerberos authentication.

During these attacks, attackers often request Kerberos tickets for an account's service principal name (SPN). They then decrypt the tickets to get plaintext credentials associated with the account. Alternatively, they can perform the pass-the-ticket technique to authenticate directly without having to decrypt the obtained tickets.

90.name: Suspicious service launched
